guard: the mesh handler's durable conclave recovers by derivation: the channel derives from the step's request id, the plan is bound before a row is written, a re-entered open converges from the recorded plan alone, the close releases exactly what the open created, an absent member is the effect's own catchable L4002, and a cancelled conclave's membership is released by the discharge
why: Lane F durable-actions step 3 (2026-09-02): `conclave` leaves the not-yet-durable seam and
performs as durable membership rows over core's channel and members registries. Each recovery
and permission half has a mutant: the resume short-circuit that makes recovery presence-free
(MC1), the incarnation pin in presence resolution (MC2), the joined-by-us discrimination that
protects a resident membership (MC3), the close's release (MC4), the discharge arm for a
cancelled subtree (MC5), the minted registry row's teardown (MC6), the catchable L4002 class
(MC7), and the re-execute guard that keeps a landed row's join cursor still (MC8).
All mutants live in ../src/mesh-handler.ts, imported by the suite through the relative source
path — no build sits between the mutation and the run.

mutations.cell: the re-entered open returns the same channel with the member's presence gone
mutations.note: The recovery contract inverted: a resume re-resolves presence instead of executing the recorded plan, so a member that died since the crash makes the re-entry fail where the plan would have converged. Measured 2026-09-02: exactly one red (the re-open rejects with the L4002 the plan exists to avoid); 38 passed.
